discovery.title: A brief AI assist may change what happens when the help disappears
discovery.summary: A randomized study involving 1,222 participants tested AI assistance on fraction problems and reading comprehension. UC Berkeley reports that participants’ accuracy and persistence fell when AI access was removed; the updated paper was presented at the Conference on Language Modeling in October.([vcresearch.berkeley.edu](https://vcresearch.berkeley.edu/news/using-ai-just-10-minutes-erodes-your-ability-persist-hard-things?utm_source=openai))
discovery.why_it_matters: The result raises questions for classrooms and workplaces about whether AI tools should simply deliver answers or help people build skills they can use without the tools. The study’s tasks and design do not establish that every kind of AI use has the same effect.([vcresearch.berkeley.edu](https://vcresearch.berkeley.edu/news/using-ai-just-10-minutes-erodes-your-ability-persist-hard-things?utm_source=openai))

discovery.title: Some ocean “snow” carries far more carbon downward than other particles
discovery.summary: A study published October 8 found that high-viscosity marine-snow particles transported more than six times as much carbon to the deep ocean as low-viscosity particles. Researchers used fluorescent dyes and 3D imaging to track how bacteria alter the particles.([scripps.ucsd.edu](https://scripps.ucsd.edu/news/gooier-marine-snow-better-it-transporting-carbon-new-study-finds?utm_source=openai))
discovery.why_it_matters: Marine snow helps move carbon from surface waters into the deep ocean. Its physical properties may influence how much carbon stays out of the atmosphere, adding detail to estimates of the ocean carbon sink.([scripps.ucsd.edu](https://scripps.ucsd.edu/news/gooier-marine-snow-better-it-transporting-carbon-new-study-finds?utm_source=openai))

discovery.title: Artemis astronauts reported seeing flashes from impacts on the Moon
discovery.summary: NASA says the Artemis II crew saw impact flashes on the Moon’s far side during the mission’s lunar flyby. The observations offer a rare human-witnessed view of meteoroid impacts and may help researchers understand the lunar impact environment.([svs.gsfc.nasa.gov](https://svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/?utm_source=openai))
discovery.why_it_matters: The Moon lacks an atmosphere that burns up small incoming debris, so estimating impact activity matters for planning exposed equipment and future surface operations. The sightings are observations, not a complete estimate of impact risk.([nasa.gov](https://www.nasa.gov/podcasts/curious-universe/artemis-ii-circles-moon/?utm_source=openai))

discovery.title: Research links how long chimpanzee mothers carry dead infants to age and cause of death
discovery.summary: An Oxford study published September 16 analyzed 83 published cases across 15 sites. It found that older infants and those reported to have died from disease were carried longer on average; the authors caution that this behavior does not necessarily mean mothers fail to recognize death.([ox.ac.uk](https://www.ox.ac.uk/news/2026-09-16-why-do-some-chimpanzee-mothers-carry-their-dead-infants-for-months?utm_source=openai))
discovery.why_it_matters: Comparative research on primate behavior can inform questions about attachment and the evolution of human responses to death, while the evidence does not justify assuming chimpanzees understand death exactly as humans do.([ox.ac.uk](https://www.ox.ac.uk/news/2026-09-16-why-do-some-chimpanzee-mothers-carry-their-dead-infants-for-months?utm_source=openai))

discovery.title: Engineers found a way to keep Voyager 2’s science instruments operating longer
discovery.summary: NASA reported in August that a power-management change should let Voyager 2 continue operating three science instruments longer than previously expected, avoiding another instrument shutdown that otherwise would have been needed before the end of 2026. The development is useful context, but it falls outside the requested 24–36-hour window.([science.nasa.gov](https://science.nasa.gov/blogs/voyager/2026/08/04/nasa-engineers-help-prolong-voyager-2s-science-mission/?utm_source=openai))
discovery.why_it_matters: Aging spacecraft can keep returning science when engineers find ways to conserve scarce power, extending the value of missions far beyond their original design horizon.([science.nasa.gov](https://science.nasa.gov/blogs/voyager/2026/08/04/nasa-engineers-help-prolong-voyager-2s-science-mission/?utm_source=openai))
